acceptance: Research how Stripe, GitHub, Vercel, Coinbase, Cloudflare and Linear confirm sensitive actions: what they protect, what proof they ask for, how long it lasts, and how it looks. Notes in docs/research with sources.

The proof is the easiest the user has (a passkey before an email code), and one confirmation covers the next protected changes for the whole window.
The code input in the confirmation looks and behaves like the kit's CodeInput on the sign-in page; find why it differs in the dialog and fix it there.

tasks.behavior: Tokens sent to the invoice receiver factory can be returned by the refund authority

Contract tests and the fuzz and invariant suites cover it; docs/contracts/rules.md and operations.md describe it; it ships before the first mainnet deploy.
A receiver's refundable() reads 0 off its intended chain, as factory.status does and refund() allows (audit 2026-11-04); a test covers it.
notes: 2026-11-04 Audit 2026-11-04: InvoiceReceiver.refundable() returns the balance on a wrong chain where refund() reverts. Fix: return 0 when block.chainid != intendedChainId. Any receiver change moves the factory's CREATE2 address (vectors test fails), so it ships with this task's redeploy.

tasks.behavior: Faster pages, scans and worker rounds from the two audits, with the same results
acceptance: The transactions page selects its rows before it joins invoices, labels and rates, and answers the same rows
The worker reads one transaction's receiver transfer logs once per scan, however many events it has
Email, reminders, retainers, ECB rates and prices run apart from chain rounds, so a slow provider never delays payment detection
Idle webhook senders share one poll of the queue instead of each polling it
The backend e2e tests build the binaries once per run
The app reads balances for the Receive sheet only while it is open
Typing in the clients search and moving over the balance chart or a combobox do no per-row work they already did
The pay page's clock stops once the checkout can take no more money
notes: 2026-11-04 review fail by reviewer: Two blocking findings. 1) Pay page: clockRuns (apps/web/src/features/pay/lib/pay.ts:158) stops the clock when the API says closed, but payState still needs it in the checking state: the delayed flag compares now with the deposit block time. A confirmed but unbooked deposit on a checkout the API has closed now never shows the delay note; a scratch test gave clockRuns false, delayed false at close and true 10 minutes later. Keep the clock running while the state is checking (or while any time-based field can still change). 2) Clients search (apps/web/src/features/clients/components/clients-table.tsx:40): useDeferredValue without a memoized table. Each keystroke's urgent render still re-renders every DataTable row with the old rows, then the deferred render renders them again, so acceptance 7 is not met for clients and no measurement backs it. Memoize the table on rows or drop the deferral. Minor: transfers.go:156 hardcodes chain_family 'evm' where the old join was family-agnostic; e2e TestMain leaks the shared bin dir when a test panics (t.TempDir cleaned it before); balance-chart.tsx writes the dateLabel default twice. Transfers page, outflow cache, housekeeping loop and shutdown order, webhook wake poller, e2e build, Receive balances, chart memo and combobox memo look correct; activity, watcher and webhook tests pass with -race; pay, clients, receive and balances vitest pass.

2026-11-04 review fail by reviewer: One blocking finding. Pay page (apps/web/src/features/pay/components/pay-invoice.tsx:236): useNow(clockRuns(answer)) reads the top-level invoice, but the page shows payState(withOption(answer, picked)) from line 258. On an unlocked multi-option invoice the API has closed, late money to the picked option B does not lock it (ledger/process.go chooses only on-time money). Option A has no deposits, so clockRuns(answer) is false while option B is in checking. Its delay note then never appears if the page was open before the 5-minute mark. A scratch test gave clockRuns(answer) false, clockRuns(shown) true, delayed false at mount and true 10 minutes later. Fix: call useNow(clockRuns(invoice)) after the useMemo, with a test on a picked option. Minor: docs/backend/architecture.md:62 still says the 16 webhook workers each poll idle queues every second; now one shared poll wakes them. e2e TestMain (gate_test.go:367) leaks the bin dir when a test panics. balance-chart.tsx writes the dateLabel default twice (220, 253). Checked and correct: transfers.go per-wallet LATERAL page gives the same rows, order, ties, cursor pages and filters (profile_wallets is unique per family and address; outer join re-applies profile and reorged filters); outflows cache keys on block, token and receiver, the same inputs as the old read; housekeeping loop stops before the lock and pool close; webhook wake poller is a superset of claimable work; single e2e build; Receive balances only while open; chart, combobox and clients memo. activity, watcher, webhook and httpapi search tests pass with -race; pay, clients, balances, receive and app-shell vitest pass.

2026-11-04 review pass by reviewer: Nothing blocks. The pay page now runs the clock from the shown option (pay-invoice.tsx:259), and the clock stops only when no shown value depends on time: closed by the API and not checking, or paid or settled. Confirming counts from readAt, not now. The architecture.md webhook line is fixed. Transfers page gives the same rows, order, ties, cursor and filters (one wallet per profile and family). The outflow cache keys on the same block, token and receiver inputs. Housekeeping stops before the lock and pool close. The webhook poll never does more work than the old per-sender poll. Receive balances, chart table, combobox and clients memo are correct. Minor: api.md:116 and :133 still say reminders and retainers run each worker round. Housekeeping no longer waits for the lock ping, which architecture.md:119 describes; each task is safe to run twice. matchesClient (clients.ts:53) still folds every client and the query on each keystroke. No test covers clockRuns on a picked option. The two minors left on purpose remain. activity, watcher and webhook pass with -race; pay, clients, balances, receive, app-shell and ui-web forms vitest pass.

tasks.behavior: New users set up their profile in short onboarding steps instead of one choice screen
acceptance: Onboarding asks the use, one details step per new freelancer or business profile, accepted test tokens, an optional passkey, then shows one first action per goal.
POST /v1/me/onboarding takes optional profile names and still creates profiles only once; details, tokens and website save through their own APIs.
The address is /app/onboarding with no ?next, the page asked for still opens after setup, and the logo sits where landing and sign-in put it.
Each step shows its number and progress, Back on the left and the main action on the right, full width on top on phones, in both themes.
notes: 2026-11-05 review fail by reviewer: Blocking: (1) first-run.tsx:271 picks the landing profile with landingProfile(profiles, after), but the app shell passes live profiles that already hold the new ones after POST onboarding, so the finish screen says 'Your account is ready' and Go to overview opens the personal profile instead of the new freelancer or business profile (D-73). Reproduced with FirstRun fed from useSignUpQuery; first-run.test.tsx passes a fixed profiles prop, so it misses this. Keep the profiles from the start of the run. (2) first-run.tsx:52 websiteOrigin accepts http://[::1], underscores and a leading hyphen, which profile/stores.go origin() refuses. The store PUT then fails after the profiles exist, Back is hidden (line 320), so every retry fails with the generic error. Match the backend rule. Notes: ready-step.tsx:34 and :50 use raw buttons where the kit rule asks for a kit control; ready-step.tsx:63 faucet link opens a new tab without saying so; settings-screen.tsx:50 still repeats the passkey string now in PRIVY_PASSKEY; PROJECT.md D-53 still quotes the old question and choice names; openapi.yaml:4273 says names are ignored once onboarded, but a bad name still gets 422; a failed token load lets Continue save without tokens.
